```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>",
  fig.width = 6, fig.height = 5)
library(stream)
set.seed(1000)
```

The package `stream` provides the reference implementation of the DBSTREAM
algorithm (Hahsler and Bolaños, 2016), a density-based data steam clustering algorithm
that uses density between micro-clusters via a shared density graph to form larger
clusters.

## Prepare a reproducible stream

The Bars and Gaussians generator contains two Gaussian clusters and two
rectangular clusters with different densities, plus noise. Store 1500 points in
memory so that plots and experiments can reuse exactly the same data.

```{r data}
stream <- DSD_Memory(DSD_BarsAndGaussians(noise = 0.05), n = 10000)
plot(stream, n = 1000)
```

Plotting a stream consumes points. Resetting the memory stream puts its cursor
back at the first point. We will use the first 1000 points for training and the
remaining 500 for evaluation.

```{r reset}
reset_stream(stream)
```

## DBSTREAM

The radius `r` controls the scale of the micro-clusters. A smaller radius can
preserve finer structure but usually requires more micro-clusters. Choose it
relative to the scale of the features; the value below is specific to this data.
With `shared_density = TRUE`, DBSTREAM records points shared by overlapping
micro-clusters. Reclustering uses this evidence to decide which micro-clusters
belong together. The parameter `alpha` controls the minimum shared-density
proportion needed to connect them.

```{r train}
dbstream<- DSC_DBSTREAM(r = 1, shared_density = TRUE, alpha = 0.3, minweight = .1)
update(dbstream, stream, n = 5000)
dbstream
```

Updating the clustering with 5000 points from the stream creates micro-clusters. 
We can visual the clustering. Red bubbles are the micro-clusters where the size 
shows how many data points they represent. The shared density is shown as black
lines. Wider lines represent more shared density. The macro-clusters represent 
micro clusters connected by sufficient shared density and are shown by big blue 
crosses.

```{r inspect}
plot(dbstream, dsd = stream, type = "both", shared_density = TRUE, n = 500)
```


DBSTREAM is able to identify the four clusters.

## Follow changing data

DBSTREAM fades older observations using `lambda`. Increasing it makes the model
forget faster. `gaptime` determines how often weak micro-clusters and weak
shared-density entries are removed, and `Cm` controls the minimum micro-cluster
weight. These settings interact with the stream's speed of change and arrival
rate.

## References

Hahsler, M., and Bolaños, M. (2016). Clustering data streams based on shared
density between micro-clusters. *IEEE Transactions on Knowledge and Data
Engineering*, 28(6), 1449–1461.

Hahsler, M., Bolaños, M., and Forrest, J. (2017). Introduction to stream: An
extensible framework for data stream clustering research with R.
*Journal of Statistical Software*, 76(14), 1–50. doi:10.18637/jss.v076.i14.
